messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Telugu, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

**Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition for Telugu (per‑token)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement (Telugu) | |-------------|----------------------|------------------------------| | **Tant'** | Intensifier of “amara” (so) | `అంత` (adv.) – placed before the adjective to convey “so”. **Literal back‑translation:** “so”. | | **è** (copula) | Links implicit subject “it” with predicate adjective | `అది` (pron., neuter) + `ఉంది` (verb, 3rd sg, pres., copular). **Literal back‑translation:** “it is”. | | **amara** | Predicate adjective “bitter” describing the subject | `కోపంగా` (adj., fem.) – agrees with the neuter pronoun in meaning. **Literal back‑translation:** “bitter”. | | **che** (comparative conjunction) | Introduces comparative clause | `కంటే` (post‑position) – marks the comparative relation. **Literal back‑translation:** “than”. | | **poco** | Degree adverb “little”, indicating slight increase | `కొంచెం` (adv.) – modifies the comparative adjective. **Literal back‑translation:** “little”. | | **è** (copula in comparative) | Links “death” with comparative predicate | `ఉంది` (verb, 3rd sg, pres., copular) attached to “death”. **Literal back‑translation:** “is”. | | **più** | Comparative adverb “more” | `అధికంగా` (adv., comparative) – expresses “more”. **Literal back‑translation:** “more”. | | **morte** | Noun “death”, the term that exceeds “bitter” | `మరణం` (noun, neuter) – subject of the comparative clause. **Literal back‑translation:** “death”. | | **;** | Clause boundary | `,` (punctuation) – separates clauses. **Literal back‑translation:** “,”. | | **ma** | Coordinating conjunction “but” | `కాని` (conj.) – connects to the next clause. **Literal back‑translation:** “but”. | | **per** | Preposition marking purpose “in order to” | `కోసం` (post‑position) – attaches to infinitive verb. **Literal back‑translation:** “for”. | | **trattar** | Infinitive “to treat/discuss” | `చర్చించడానికి` (verb, infinitive, purpose) – conveys “to discuss”. **Literal back‑translation:** “to discuss”. | | **del** | Partitive “of the” (di + il) | `సంబంధించి` (post‑position) – links verb to object “good”. **Literal back‑translation:** “of”. | | **ben** | Noun “good” (object of discussion) | `మంచి` (noun, neuter) – object of `చర్చించడానికి`. **Literal back‑translation:** “good”. | | **ch'** | Relative pronoun “that” | `అది` (rel. pron., neuter) – introduces relative clause. **Literal back‑translation:** “that”. | | **i'** | Pronoun “I” | `నేను` (pron., 1st sg) – subject of relative clause. **Literal back‑translation:** “I”. | | **vi** | Locative adverb “there” | `అక్కడ` (adv.) – locative complement. **Literal back‑translation:** “there”. | | **trovai** | Past tense “found” (passato remoto) | `కనుగొన్నాను` (verb, 1st sg, aorist) – perfective past. **Literal back‑translation:** “found”. | | **,** | Clause separator | `,` (punctuation). **Literal back‑translation:** “,”. | | **dirò** | Future tense “I will tell” | `చెప్పుతాను` (verb, 1st sg, future) – expresses future intention. **Literal back‑translation:** “I will tell”. | | **de** | Partitive “of the” (di + le) | `సంబంధించి` (post‑position) – links verb to noun phrase. **Literal back‑translation:** “of”. | | **l'altre** | Determiner “the other” (plural) | `ఇతర` (adj., plural) – modifies “things”. **Literal back‑translation:** “other”. | | **cose** | Noun “things” (plural) | `వస్తువులు` (noun, plural) – direct object of `చెప్పుతాను`. **Literal back‑translation:** “things”. | | **ch'** | Relative pronoun “that” | `అవి` (rel. pron., plural) – introduces relative clause. **Literal back‑translation:** “that”. | | **i'** | Pronoun “I” | `నేను` (pron., 1st sg) – subject of relative clause. **Literal back‑translation:** “I”. | | **v'** | Locative adverb “there” | `అక్కడ` (adv.) – locative complement. **Literal back‑translation:** “there”. | | **ho** | Auxiliary “have” (present) | `ఉన్నాను` (auxiliary, 1st sg, pres.) – forms perfect. **Literal back‑translation:** “have”. | | **scorte** | Past participle “seen” (scorgere) | `చూసిన` (participle, neuter, plural) – combined with auxiliary to form perfect. **Literal back‑translation:** “seen”. |
**Notes on Comparative Ordering & Degree (Line 7)** - The Telugu clause must preserve the ordering **death > bitter** with a slight degree: `మరణం (death) కొంచెం (little) ఎక్కువగా (more) ఉంటుంది (is)` → literal back‑translation “death is a little more”. - The comparative marker `కంటే` is omitted because the structure “X అధికంగా ఉంది” already encodes “X is more”. The adverb `కొంచెం` explicitly marks the slightness of the increase.

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: అంతకోపంగా మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది / మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది / కోపం కన్నా మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువ - Line 8: మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను / చర్చించడానికి నేను అక్కడ మంచి కనుగొన్నాను / నేను అక్కడ మంచి కనుగొన్నాను - Line 9: నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు చెప్పుతాను / అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు నేను చెప్పుతాను / ఇతర విషయాలు నేను అక్కడ చూసి చెప్పుతాను

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Telugu lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - అంతకోపంగా మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already contains the comparative marker, degree adverb, and copula.
**Target Text:** అంతకోపంగా మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది;
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra words required; the infinitive చర్చించడానికి expresses purpose and the relative clause is embedded.
**Target Text:** మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు చెప్పుతాను
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional morphology needed; the phrase includes the future verb చెప్పుతాను and the relative clause.
**Target Text:** నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు చెప్పుతాను.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line #**: 7 **Target Text**: అంతకోపంగా మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది; **Back-Translation**: “So bitter, death is a little more.” **Reference Translation**: “So bitter is it that death is little more.” **Checks**: End Punct OK | Coverage OK | Meaning Drift OK | Comparative Orientation OK | Hallucination OK **Corrected Target Text**:
- **Line #**: 8 **Target Text**: మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్నాను, **Back-Translation**: “To discuss about the good, I found there.” **Reference Translation**: “But in order to treat of the good that there I found.” **Checks**: End Punct OK | Coverage FAIL | Meaning Drift FAIL | Comparative Orientation N/A | Hallucination OK **Corrected Target Text**: కానీ నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి,
- **Line #**: 9 **Target Text**: నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు చెప్పుతాను. **Back-Translation**: “I will tell the other things I saw there.” **Reference Translation**: “I will tell of the other things that I have seen there.” **Checks**: End Punct OK | Coverage OK | Meaning Drift OK | Comparative Orientation N/A | Hallucination OK **Corrected Target Text**:
``` అంతకోపంగా మరణం కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది; కాని నేను అక్కడ కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి, నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు చెప్పుతాను. ```
